topic: NVIDIA-Certified Associate AI Model and Application Development (NCA-AMAD) exam preparation - NVIDIA's newest associate credential for entry-level AI developers, covering how AI models are built, customized, served, and consumed as applications: models and model types, model customization and fine-tuning, inference concepts, data processing and the data flywheel, agentic AI, NVIDIA AI Enterprise and Blueprints, sizing and configuration, and physical AI
cert_name: NVIDIA-Certified Associate: AI Model & Application Development
exam_format: Online, remote-proctored exam delivered via Certiverse: 50-60 multiple-choice questions, 60 minutes, pass/fail (passing score not publicly disclosed). Includes a hands-on lab component. Certification is valid for two years; recertification is by retaking the current exam. No formal prerequisites; NVIDIA recommends its 'AI Model and Application Development Fundamentals' course but the exam can be taken on its own (exam-only). A Certiverse account is required to register. Confirm current pricing and format on the NVIDIA certification site.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Entry-level AI developers, software engineers, and technical practitioners who want to prove they understand how modern AI models are customized, served, and consumed as applications on the NVIDIA stack. Pairs naturally with the catalog's other NVIDIA associate credentials (NCA-AIIO, NCA-GENL, NCA-GENM, NCA-ADS) and is a strong on-ramp to the NCP professional track - cross-sell those in the funnel. No deep ML research background required, but comfort with core AI/ML vocabulary and basic Python is assumed.
author: Aseem Mankotia

media.image_style: Clean modern tech illustration, NVIDIA-adjacent palette (deep green #76b900 accents on dark slate/charcoal with white space), GPU/data-center/neural-network/pipeline motifs, abstract and professional, NO text, NO words, NO numbers, NO logos, NO brand marks

domains.name: Agentic AI
domains.notes: The single heaviest-weighted topic. AI agents and agentic workflows: tool use/function calling, planning and reasoning loops, multi-step and multi-agent orchestration, memory, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as an agentic pattern, guardrails, and how NVIDIA frames agentic applications (NeMo, NIM microservices, Blueprints). Scenario questions on choosing when an agent vs a single model call is appropriate.

domains.name: Data Processing and the Data Flywheel
domains.notes: Data pipelines for AI applications: ingestion, cleaning, curation, synthetic data, embeddings and vector stores, and the 'data flywheel' concept (production data improving models over time). Data quality, governance, and feedback loops that drive continuous model improvement.

domains.name: Inference Concepts
domains.notes: Serving and running models in production: inference vs training, latency/throughput tradeoffs, batching, quantization and precision, KV cache, inference servers (Triton), NIM microservices, and optimizing cost/performance for deployed AI applications.

domains.name: Model Customization and Fine-Tuning Concepts
domains.notes: Adapting foundation models: prompt engineering vs RAG vs fine-tuning vs full training, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA/PEFT), instruction tuning, alignment (RLHF/DPO at a conceptual level), and choosing the right customization technique for a given use case and budget.

domains.name: Models and Model Types
domains.notes: The landscape of AI models: LLMs, multimodal models, embedding models, diffusion/generative vision models, transformers and attention at a conceptual level, open vs proprietary models, and matching model type to task.

domains.name: NVIDIA AI Enterprise and Blueprints Overview
domains.notes: The NVIDIA AI software ecosystem at an associate level: NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NIM microservices, NeMo, and NVIDIA Blueprints (reference workflows for common agentic/GenAI applications). What each component is for and how they fit together to build and deploy AI applications.

domains.name: Sizing and Configuration
domains.notes: Right-sizing compute for AI workloads: GPU memory and model size, selecting hardware/instances for training vs inference, scaling, and basic cost/capacity planning for AI applications.

domains.name: Physical AI
domains.notes: Introductory physical-AI concepts: AI that perceives and acts in the real world, robotics and autonomous systems, simulation (Isaac/Omniverse at a conceptual level), and digital twins. Smallest weight - keep coverage proportional but accurate.

extra_guidance: NCA-AMAD is NVIDIA's NEWEST associate certification (not previously in this catalog) and the only net-new NVIDIA exam as of late 2026 - position it as the fresh, in-demand on-ramp to NVIDIA's AI-developer track. Exam facts to use: 50-60 multiple-choice questions, 60 minutes, pass/fail, $125, delivered via Certiverse, includes a hands-on lab, valid two years, exam-only path available (recommended course not required). Use the OFFICIAL topic weights above verbatim (they are NVIDIA's published exam weights, not editorial) - emphasize Agentic AI (17%) and Data Processing/Data Flywheel (17%) most, Physical AI (6%) least. Keep content vendor-accurate to the NVIDIA stack (NeMo, NIM, Triton, NVIDIA AI Enterprise, Blueprints, RAPIDS where relevant) but teach transferable concepts so the course is useful beyond NVIDIA tooling. Chapter 1 = exam overview + the AI-application mental model (train -> customize -> serve -> consume). Chapters map to the 8 domains in weight order; include a dedicated agentic-AI chapter and a RAG/data-flywheel chapter. Labs are conceptual/architecture walkthroughs (design a RAG pipeline, pick a fine-tuning strategy, size a GPU for an inference workload, sketch an agentic app with NIM/Blueprints) - no paid cloud required. Final chapter = full exam simulation with a 60-minute / 50-60-question time-management strategy. Practice questions scenario-based with plausible distractors; scan the practice bank per the pipeline compliance rules (no 'guaranteed pass' / 'first attempt' language). Marketing angle: 'Master NVIDIA's newest AI-developer credential - complete NCA-AMAD prep covering agentic AI, RAG, fine-tuning, and inference.' Cross-sell the other NVIDIA associate + NCP courses in this catalog.
